headline: First uranium consignment arrives in Dhaka from Russia
summary: The first cargo plane carrying nuclear fuel for the Rooppur Nuclear Power Plant has landed, marking a critical step toward the plant's operational status.
details: The first cargo plane carrying nuclear fuel for the Rooppur Nuclear Power Plant arrived in Dhaka from Russia on Friday night. The flight landed at Hazrat Shahjalal International Airport around 11:44 PM under international security guidelines.
Following the unloading process, the nuclear fuel will be transported to the project site in Rooppur under special security arrangements by the Bangladesh Army.

Golam Mahbub, chief of administration of the Rooppur Nuclear Power Plant, stated that a total of nine flights will deliver more than 200 assembled fuel elements, including 163 assemblies for Unit-2, by December.
Highway police have been instructed to ensure security and maintain clear lanes on the highway for the smooth and safe movement of the uranium convoy to the project site.
This delivery follows a previous attempt on September 24, which was postponed due to a lack of airspace clearance.
caption:
Nuclear fuel has finally landed in Bangladesh. The first shipment of uranium from Russia has arrived in Dhaka.

The first cargo plane carrying nuclear fuel for the Rooppur Nuclear Power Plant arrived in Dhaka from Russia on Friday night. The flight landed at Hazrat Shahjalal International Airport around 11:44 PM under international security guidelines.

Following the unloading process, the nuclear fuel will be transported to the project site in Rooppur under special security arrangements by the Bangladesh Army.

Golam Mahbub, chief of administration of the Rooppur Nuclear Power Plant, stated that a total of nine flights will deliver more than 200 assembled fuel elements, including 163 assemblies for Unit-2, by December.

Highway police have been instructed to ensure security and maintain clear lanes on the highway for the smooth and safe movement of the uranium convoy to the project site.

This delivery follows a previous attempt on September 24, which was postponed due to a lack of airspace clearance.

headline: 635 crimes: Teen gangs in Chattogram shift political patronage to stay active
summary: Police report that gang leaders who were previously backed by Awami League leaders are now seeking shelter with BNP leaders to maintain their influence.
details: In Chattogram, teen gangs are adapting to the political shift after August 5, 2024. Gang leaders who were once protected by Awami League leaders are now seen associating with BNP and its affiliate organizations to avoid legal action and maintain power.

Police records show that teen gangs have been involved in at least 635 crimes in the city over the last seven and a half years, including 39 murders. Currently, at least 45 areas of the city are plagued by these gangs, with 11 major gangs like MBS, KB, and Python dominating the scene.
The violence continues to escalate. Last week, a 16-year-old boy named Md. Hridoy was killed in a clash between the 'Five Star' and 'Seven Star' gangs in the Wireless Colony area of Pahartali.

Local residents and teachers report living in fear, as gang members are used to control drug trade routes and intimidate residents. Some residents claim that gang leaders like Wakil Hossain, alias Boga, continue to operate despite being expelled from political party positions.

Chattogram Metropolitan Police (CMP) Commissioner Hassan Mo. Shawkat Ali stated that police alone cannot control these gangs. He emphasized that political leaders must stop providing shelter to these criminals to break the cycle of violence.

The BNP's member secretary for the city, Nazimur Rahman, stated that some gang members are now associating with their party workers, which is damaging the party's image. He claimed that those providing such shelter are being warned.
